subject: general
question: Which enzyme in the pancreatic juice helps in breaking down fats?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lipase.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lipase,** 

 
 
• **Triglycerides are broken down by a class of enzymes called lipases into free fatty acids and glycerol.**
 
• They are present and functional in a variety of tissues; for instance, hepatic lipases are found in the liver, hormone-sensitive lipases in adipocytes, lipoprotein lipase is found on the surface of vascular endothelial cells, and pancreatic lipase is found in the small intestine.
 
• This enzyme functions in conjunction with the bile your liver produces.
 
• Your body will have problems absorbing fat and the crucial fat-soluble vitamins if you don't have enough lipase (A, D, E, K).
 
• Poor fat absorption is characterized by diarrhea and greasdiarrheay bowel motions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protease,**

 
 
• Proteases have more specialised uses in the extraction of mucopolysaccharides and carbohydrate gums, which are nonprotein compounds made from animal or plant extracts.
 
• Proteases can be employed to dissolve keratin-containing materials, such as feather debris, to provide protein concentrates for animal diets. Streptomyces species' alkaline proteases have potent keratinolytic activity as well.
 
• Your diet's protein is broken down by this enzyme.
 
• Also, it aids in defending you against microorganisms like certain bacteria and yeast that could reside in your intestines.
 
 
 
• **Amylase,**
 
 
• Any member of the class of enzymes known as amylases is responsible for catalysing the breakdown of starch into smaller carbohydrate molecules like maltose (a molecule composed of two glucose molecules). 
 
• Alpha-amylase is present in many biological things.
 
• Ptyalin, an alpha-amylase produced by salivary glands in the digestive tracts of humans and many other mammals, is secreted into the small intestine by pancreatic amylase.
 
• The undigested carbs may cause diarrhea if you don't have enough amylase.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin,**
 
 
• Pepsin, a potent digestive enzyme found in gastric juice, breaks down proteins found in foods including meat, eggs, seeds, and dairy products.
 
• The mature active version of the inactive protein pepsinogen is called pepsin.
 
• Pepsinogen is produced and stored by glands in the mucous membrane lining of the stomach. Pepsinogen is released into the stomach under the influence of vagus nerve impulses and the hormonal secretions gastrin and secretin, where it is combined with hydrochloric acid and quickly transformed into the active enzyme pepsin.
